summary: This is a documentation-only change (ai-os/MASTER_INDEX.yaml drift fix + two new YAML artifacts: a 145-item gap analysis and a compact 10-phase status refresh) with no code, migration, schema, workflow, or security-path changes, so tier1 is correctly classified and blast radius is genuinely low. The task's central, load-bearing claim -- that the prior MASTER_INDEX status entry was stale because phases 1-3 (compliance-tracker PRs #559/#560/#561) actually merged and phase 4 (PR #562) is open/unmerged -- was independently re-verified against live GitHub via `gh pr view` during this review and is accurate; the corrected MASTER_INDEX status, next_phase pointer, and evidence_chain are all consistent with real repo state. All three YAML files parse cleanly and the phase plan's verification_command per phase is sound and runnable. One real correctness defect was found and should be fixed in a fast follow-up rather than blocking this merge: the gap analysis's own headline_finding narrative claims 15 fully_implemented / 47 partially_implemented / 43 not_implemented among the 105 non-YCML items, but mechanically tallying the verdict field across the actual items[] array yields 16 / 34 / 55 -- a material arithmetic mismatch (off by 1, 13, and 12 respectively) in the document's flagship summary stat, even though the per-item evidence text and verdicts themselves appear internally consistent and well-cited. Given this is a purely additive knowledge artifact with independently-verified core facts and no execution/deploy risk, approving with the issue flagged for correction is appropriate rather than rejecting outright.
issues: headline_finding block in ai-os/OWNER_ENGINE_TASK2_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-07-27.yaml states '15 are now fully_implemented ... 47 are partially_implemented ... 43 remain not_implemented' for the 105 non-YCML items, but the actual verdict fields across items[] tally to 16 fully_implemented / 34 partially_implemented / 55 not_implemented -- the headline stat should be corrected to match the real per-item data (or the per-item verdicts corrected if the headline numbers were the intended target), since this summary is what future dispatch/planning sessions will trust at a glance.
